cards.note: In Okinawa, utility pole plates have numbers from 1 to 6 (except 5) at the top, which can help with region guessing. For example, as you can see in the image, the south of Okinawa is 2, the north is 6, and the Okinawa Islands are 1.

• In the Miyako Islands, utility pole plates have the number 7 at the top, while in the Yaeyama Islands they have the number 8.
  • Also, Road 390 runs through both island groups but nowhere else, and the landscape with red soil and sugarcane is almost unique to the Yaeyama and Miyako Islands.

• In the Yaeyama Islands, utility pole plates have the number 8 at the top, while in the Miyako Islands they have the number 7.
  • Also, Road 390 runs through both island groups but nowhere else, and the landscape with red soil and sugarcane is almost unique to the Yaeyama and Miyako Islands.
You’ll find these Apple guardrails in Aomori, mostly in Aomori City (I’m not even sure if you can find them anywhere else in the prefecture)
Aso Caldera in Kyushu is one of the world’s largest volcanic calderas. Its vast grasslands, steep green slopes, and active volcano make the landscape strikingly different from most of Japan.

Cycling routes in Ehime have a continuous outside white line and inside blue line. If either line is broken or dashed, it's probably not an Ehime route. They're mostly along the coast, but can be inland too. Exceptions are rare. There are also many routes like this on nearby islands such as Osaki Shimozima and Toyoshima (which are not part of Ehime).

In Tochigi, you can often spot a small colorful rectangle sticker (green, blue, white, etc.) on the back of road signs. Warning: A similar meta appears in Akita and Nagasaki, you can see the differences in the images. Update: In Fukui, you can also find something similar, so try to identify the region first.
These traditional gassho-zukuri villages can be found in Shirakawa-go and Gokayama, along with their surrounding areas. I also spotted some in Yamanashi, around Lake Saiko

In Kyushu, especially in Miyazaki and Oita, you can find this green ring or sticker-like band on guardrail posts. It's rarely seen in Fukuoka, Saga, or Nagasaki, and appears to be even more uncommon in the other Kyushu prefectures.

"Saga Green Reflector" are commonly seen on poles at major intersections. Warning : A green reflector can commonly be found in Nagano Prefecture, but this one is different. I’ll add it in a future update.

You can find this plate in Hakone. There’s also a brown version which should be unique to Hakone, so if you see them together you can pretty safely guess Hakone. I did spot the "threaded" plate once in Yamanashi, but it seems to be extremely rare.

Again, I’m not 100% sure, so if you see it somewhere else please let me know.

This pole top, which looks like two little hearts from far away, is mostly Hokuriku (~90%). I've seen a couple in Shikoku, but it seems extremely rare. Warning: Chubu pole tops can bait you — takes time to tell them apart from a distance.

cards.a: Kanji - 県 - 市 - 町 - 道
cards.note: These kanji are pretty important — they help you recognize names like 'Yamaguchi Prefecture' (山口県) or 'Okayama City' (岡山市). The kanji for 'city' or 'prefecture' appears at the end of the name. You can search them on the map or learn the kanji to guess faster.

• Lake Biwa is the largest lake in Japan. It’s easy to recognize not only because of its size, but also thanks to the cherry blossoms lining parts of the shore. The area has a vibe you learn to recognize.
  • I also noticed this reflector/sticker on the guardrails, which seems to be unique to Shiga. I’m not completely sure though.

In Akita, you can often spot a small colorful square sticker (green, blue, white, etc.) on the back of road signs (often with something written on it) Warning: A similar meta appears in Nagasaki and Tochigi, you can see the differences in the images.

• Mount Hachimantai is recognizable by its mix of dead trees and conifers.

  • Coverage exists in May 2014 / May–June 2024 (with snow still visible in May) and Oct 2023 (when the trees turn yellow, making the area even easier to recognize).

  • Warning : A similar landscape can be found in Mt. Zao (between Yamagata and Miyagi) along Route 12, but the center line is yellow, not dashed white like in Hachimantai.

Let me know if you spot another similar area.
In Hokkaido, on the northern part of the west coast, you can see Mount Rishiri.
In Shizuoka, you'll find multiple white and yellow round stickers (inspection seals) on almost every sign or signpost. You shouldn't need another clue to guess the prefecture.
This orange/yellow plate or sticker is unique to Hokkaido. It's not a very important meta, but it can still be useful in no move. Don’t confuse it with the white/yellow Chūgoku plate.

In Chubu (except Yamanashi and Hokuriku), you’ll find this top pole and two others unique to the area. The fork-shaped one looks like those in Kansai and Kanto, but they’re different. (Saw a rare similar one in Akita too.) Important note : Niigata has the Kanto top pole and the 'Akita' one. Niigata is kind of weird and mixes a lot of meta. If you see something mixing a lot of meta, you’re probably in Niigata or sometimes in Nagano.
These unique red-tiled roofs are most commonly found in Chugoku, especially in the prefectures of Hiroshima and Shimane.
These striped bollards (which cover over the original) have a thinner top half, and no reflectors, and are common to the Tohoku region. They are especially common in Akita prefecture.

cards.a: Red And Yellow Striped Stickers  - Chugoku And Niigata
cards.note: Guardrail endings with these red and yellow striped stickers can commonly be found across Chugoku, except in Yamaguchi. They can also rarely be found in Niigata. (if there’s White Birch around, go to Niigata)

In Nagasaki, you can often spot a small colorful square sticker (green, blue, white, etc.) on the back of road signs. Warning: A similar meta appears in Akita and Tochigi. The biggest confusion is a Yamagata sticker that looks just like this but is always yellow. (make sure you are in Kyushu)

In Hiroshima, you can find this yellow and green reflector/sticker with a snail, the letters 'H.P.', and what seems to be a momiji leaf (or maybe something else). You’ll see it at intersections near traffic lights.
In Saitama, stoplight terminal box typically has a C.
These specific black signs with two yellow circles are found in Kagawa. Other variations can be seen, including them stacked on top of each other, or with an arrow attached above.

The Nichinan Kaigan Road (Route 220) runs from Miyazaki to Nichinan, known for its ocean views and tall palm trees dividing the lanes, though they aren't present all along the road. Warning: some roads in Okinawa and Awaji Island (especially near Iwaya on Route 28) may look similar.
This 'V' sticker is unique to Gunma Prefecture, you'll find them behind signs.
Chiba’s white and yellow reflectors can be a useful clue. Warning: some reflectors in Kanagawa and Aichi may look similar. I also found a similar-looking one in Nimi City, Okayama.

In Gunma, you’ll see these wooden signs with two yellow bands at the bottom.

I’m not 100% sure they’re unique to this prefecture, but I haven’t seen them anywhere else. Maybe double-check that you’re in Kanto before guessing Gunma (and let me know if you spot them somewhere else).
This zebra stripe band on the poles seems unique to northern Tōhoku. Personally, I’ve only seen it in Iwate and Yamagata, mostly near water and especially along the coast.
